## Execution audit

**Provenance.** All citations refer to expanded files under `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_probes/C1/development/`. Their archive is `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/work/scene_archive/bundles/ablation_r1--ours_without_probes.tar.gz`; the corresponding member is `experiments/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_probes/C1/development/` followed by the cited relative file path. Source IDs and original line numbers follow.

### French chaise room — commons_109923183

The step 3 code describes a revision in response to its own step 2 observations: closer framing, a deeper wall, a wider chaise and reduced lighting and floor reflectance. Those observations are author claims, not independently inspected images. The code explicitly acknowledges uncertain scale and camera calibration (X0221, `commons_109923183/steps/003/build.py`, lines 4–15).

The scene uses colored boxes, filleted boxes, rods, swept tubes and balls: parquet and paneling, glazing and curtain folds, a carved chaise with legs, frame, mattress, headrest and ornament, a separate pillow and label, and a cane-strand foreground chair. The chaise, pillow and label receive the same 1.25 width scaling and −16° rotation (X0221, lines 58–86, 88–152, 154–205, 222–285). Stripes, embroidery, cane and parquet are modeled geometry rather than image textures; no image-texture loading appears in this supplied script. Materials are copied per subtree and Principled roughness set to .79 or .90 where the node exists; larger meshes in selected subtrees are smoothed (X0221, lines 303–329).

The specified camera is (−.69, −5.04, 3.64), aimed at (−.19, .10, 1.02), lens 48; two area lights have powers 440 and 65, with world strength .22. Output is set to 512×384, 100%, AgX (X0221, lines 17–20, 47–49, 331–354). The task metadata also lists a 512×384 reference (X0223, `commons_109923183/task.json`, lines 2–5).

Both recorded steps 2 and 3 completed 16 samples, saved `final.png` and `scene.blend`, and report `ok: true`, null error and empty stderr; step 3’s logged render took 11.20 seconds (X0220, `commons_109923183/steps/002/result.json`, lines 2–7; X0222, `commons_109923183/steps/003/result.json`, lines 2–7). This establishes successful recorded rendering, not visual fidelity. No selection or acceptance record for this scene is supplied.

### Shipboard compartment — commons_118588033

The supplied final build models a shell, two-tone column, three-tier bunk, lockers, machinery, chair, fittings, benches, pipes and pendants as separately named composite Assets made mainly from boxes, rods and balls (X0224, `commons_118588033/build.py`, lines 61–83, 85–156, 158–226, 228–312). Its proposed revisions retain the step 2 camera while adjusting placements, pendant, exposure and floor finish; the stated prior visual mismatches are not independent measurements (X0224, lines 5–26). Compared with step 1’s nearly horizontal camera target, the final target is lower; final lens is 26 with sensor 36 (X0228, `commons_118588033/steps/001/build.py`, lines 15–18, 298; X0224, lines 23–26, 318).

The final code isolates copied materials, gives pendant diffusers emission strength 4 where available, and sets floor roughness .30. Its visible surface detail, including floor seams and locker vents, is geometry and color; no image-texture operation is shown. Four area lights, world strength .32, AgX and exposure −.85 are specified; the external runner controls output settings (X0224, lines 98–105, 158–169, 320–346, 348–382). Constructor assertions check finite positive dimensions, distinct paths and unique child keys; they do not establish physical contact. The code’s claims that feet and decks meet are intent, not a collision measurement (X0224, lines 63–83, 291–317).

Step 1 actually reports a completed 16-sample Blender render, saved image and blend, with null error and empty stderr (X0229, `commons_118588033/steps/001/result.json`, lines 2–7). The overall record reports three executions, CPU, complete status and no runtime failure; a separate selection file records step 3, although the record’s `selected` field is null (X0225, `commons_118588033/record.json`, lines 16–23, 37–57; X0226, `commons_118588033/selected.json`, lines 1–3). No step 3 execution log is supplied here.

The record marks structure, material and composite checks as passing for the aisle chair, expressly as structural/edit operability; semantic completeness and support/collision truth are null. Its reported overall score is 0.39677, SSIM 0.17160 and LPIPS 0.78965 (X0225, lines 17–34). These measurements and the selection are not independent proof of image quality. With no reference or rendered images attached, neither scene’s reconstruction quality or part contacts can be visually verified; completed rendering is distinct from a potentially poor reconstruction.
